title: From Individual Songs to Music Corpora: Evaluating Explainable Harmonic Decision-Making on HookTheory
abstract: arXiv:2610.22416v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automatic melody harmonization is often evaluated through individual compositions or data-driven corpus models. This study examines whether an explainable harmonic decision model developed for individual songs can be applied to independently collected human annotations without changing its rules. We evaluate a frozen Explainable Melody Harmonizer (EMH) on selected HookTheory excerpts containing aligned melody and chord annotations. EMH generates chord sequences from melody alone using explicit criteria for melodic compatibility, harmonic function, persistence, cadence, meter-aware segmentation, and Viterbi-like optimization. Human chords are withheld during generation and used only for post-hoc comparison.   Nineteen excerpts yielded 439 evaluable harmonic segments. Exact chord agreement reached 20.50%, chord-root agreement 31.66%, and harmonic-function agreement 47.62%, with functions assessed relative to the key inferred by EMH. Deci

translated_title: 从个体歌曲到音乐语料库：在HookTheory上评估可解释的和声决策
translated_abstract: 自动的旋律和声编配通常通过对单个作品或数据驱动的语料库模型来评估。本研究考察了一种为单个歌曲开发的可解释和声决策模型，能否在不改变其规则的情况下应用于独立收集的人类标注数据。我们在选定的包含旋律与和弦对齐标注的HookTheory片段上评估了一个冻结的可解释旋律和声编配器（EMH）。EMH仅根据旋律生成和弦序列，其使用明确的准则，包括旋律兼容性、和声功能、持续性、终止式、节拍感知分段以及类维特比优化。人类标注的和弦在生成过程中被隐藏，仅用于事后比较。十九个片段共产生了439个可评估的和声片段。和弦完全一致率达到20.50%，和弦根音一致率为31.66%，和声功能一致率为47.62%，其中和声功能是基于EMH推断出的调性来评估的。
tldr: 该研究验证了为单个歌曲设计的可解释旋律和声编配模型（EMH）无需修改规则即可直接应用于独立收集的HookTheory人类标注数据，在和弦完全匹配、根音及和声功能层面分别达到20.50%、31.66%和47.62%的一致率。
en_tdlr: This study shows that an Explainable Melody Harmonizer (EMH) designed for individual songs can be applied unchanged to independently collected HookTheory human annotations, achieving 20.50% exact chord, 31.66% chord-root, and 47.62% harmonic-function agreement.
